name: FormField
description: FormField puts a label, help text and an error or success message around a form control and wires them together, so screen readers announce the label, hint and error with the control. Library fields like Textarea use it internally; use it directly to build fields from other controls.
whenToUse: To label a control that has no label of its own, e.g. a third-party date picker.
To group related controls (switches, checkboxes) under one question with group.

whenNotToUse.text: Around InputField, Textarea or RadioGroup: they already include it.
whenNotToUse.alternative: The field’s own label, description and error props

whenNotToUse.text: For a heading over a whole form section.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Names the control (a legend for groups).

anatomy.name: Control
anatomy.description: Any input, or several for groups.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Help text, announced with the control.

anatomy.name: Message
anatomy.description: Error or success text, announced with the control.

values.meaning: One control: a label linked to it by id. Default.
Several controls answering one question: a fieldset and legend.

behavior.text: A single child element gets id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, required and disabled merged in; props the child already sets win. For controls that need the props elsewhere, pass a function child.
Inside a FormField, useFormField() returns the same control props.
With group, the fieldset’s disabled disables every control inside; description and message describe the group.

content: Label: a short noun phrase (“Email address”), not an instruction.
Description: what or how to enter, e.g. “We’ll only use this for receipts”.
Error: say what went wrong and how to fix it: “Enter a date in the future”.

guidelines.do: Give every control a visible label.
guidelines.dont: Use placeholder text as the label.
guidelines.why: Placeholders disappear while typing and often fail contrast.

guidelines.do: Use group for a set of checkboxes or switches.
guidelines.dont: Put a plain label above a group of controls.
guidelines.why: A legend names the group for screen readers; a label can point at one control only.

guidelines.do: Write errors that say how to fix the problem.
guidelines.why: People need to know what to change.

keyboard.action: From the control. Clicking the label focuses the control.

aria.when: Points at the description and message.
Set on the control when there is an error.
The control’s required attribute already says it.

wcag.how: Label, legend and descriptions are programmatically linked.
Errors are text, linked to the control and marked aria-invalid.
Every control gets a label; help text is announced.

notes: Explain the asterisk once per form, e.g. “Fields marked * are required”.

examples.title: Label any control
examples.description: The child gets id and the ARIA wiring.
examples.code:
import { FormField } from '@ds/react';

<FormField label="Start date" description="The first day of your trip." required>
  <DatePicker />
</FormField>

examples.title: Group of switches
examples.code:
import { FormField, Switch } from '@ds/react';

<FormField group label="Email me about">
  <Switch label="Comments" defaultChecked />
  <Switch label="New followers" />
</FormField>

examples.title: Render function
examples.description: Put the props where a third-party control needs them.

related.relation: Has the same label and messages built in.

changes: Groups: help text sits under the legend, and more space separates the legend from the controls.

components.name: FormField
components.description:
The control props of the nearest FormField, for building custom controls. Returns null
outside a FormField.

--form-field-gap.description: Tightest gap between tightly related items, e.g. icon and label.

--form-field-group-gap.description: Gap between related items in a group.

--form-field-label-font-family.description: Body text and most UI text.

--form-field-required-text-color.description: Tone-colored text directly on surfaces, e.g. text buttons and links.

--form-field-optional-text-color.description: Supporting text on surfaces: descriptions, metadata, placeholders.

--form-field-message-font-family.description: Body text and most UI text.

--form-field-description-text-color.description: Supporting text on surfaces: descriptions, metadata, placeholders.

--form-field-error-text-color.description: Tone-colored text directly on surfaces, e.g. text buttons and links.

--form-field-success-text-color.description: Tone-colored text directly on surfaces, e.g. text buttons and links.
